content: {"summary":"During the incident the CPU rise was modest and the main problem was the reconciliation batch using more workers than the HikariCP pool could provide, exhausting connections. The team resolved it by lowering batch parallelism and did not increase maximumPoolSize, noting that raising the pool would only let the batch consume more DB connections. Therefore bumping maximumPoolSize is not recommended mid‑incident; the focus should be on throttling the batch or separating its pool.","likely_cause":"Reconciliation batch parallelism (LEDGER_RECON_PARALLELISM) exceeds the HikariCP maximumPoolSize, causing connection exhaustion and downstream 503 errors.","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"CPU was elevated but not saturated, indicating it was not the root cause","evidence_ids":["RB-013#2"],"quote":"CPU on that pod was clearly elevated, around two thirds of its limit, but it never got close to the limit."},{"text":"Batch parallelism (24) exceeded the pool size (20), exhausting connections","evidence_ids":["RB-013#5"],"quote":"The batch's parallelism was LEDGER_RECON_PARALLELISM=24, more workers than the pool has connections."},{"text":"The incident was resolved without raising maximumPoolSize; increasing it was deemed undesirable","evidence_ids":["RB-013#6"],"quote":"We did not raise maximumPoolSize. A bigger pool would have let the batch hold even more of ledger-db."},{"text":"Recommendation is to throttle the batch rather than change the pool size","evidence_ids":["RB-013#7"],"quote":"If it's the batch, throttle the batch; don't touch the pool."}],"next_checks":["Monitor hikaricp_connections_pending after any config change","Verify the current LEDGER_RECON_PARALLELISM setting and adjust if needed","Consider creating a separate HikariCP pool for the reconciliation batch","Test the impact of increasing maximumPoolSize in a staging environment before production changes"]}
